m.c:research: First-passage times are everywhere a search has to succeed: a molecule finding a receptor, a signal crossing a network, a pest finding a trap (Chapter 07).
m.c:ukairs: Many languages are typed through an input method — software that turns typed letters into characters — or a romanisation: pinyin (romanised Chinese), Japanese romaji, Arabizi. Knowing where meaning survives the shortcut tells people when they can skip that step with an AI agent.
m.c:engine-room: The aim: move the company from trying AI to using it every day — safely, with governance built in, and with a person confirming before anything is sent, shared or approved.
m.c:on-stage: A company’s AI work is judged partly by how it presents itself — in English, on trade floors and in print — and by whether its own people can work with AI agents.
m.c:teaching: Teaching is where an explanation either works or it doesn’t: undergraduate tutorials, MSc labs, summer projects for business students.
m.c:representing: Most of what makes a PhD harder is small and fixable — once someone collects it and carries it to the room where decisions are made.
m.c:enterprise: Where traps go is still largely a judgement call; placing them well could mean fewer chemical rodenticides.
m.c:media: Work that no one sees has not quite arrived: posts, talks and videos, in two languages, are how it reaches people.
m.c:westward: It is where the question behind the later AI work first appeared: judge a tool by whether its output answers real questions, not by how it looks.
m.c:workshop: Small public tools are where new methods get tried first, at a scale where failing is cheap.
m.c:roots: The pieces were there before the PhD: random walks already in the undergraduate thesis, and a habit of speaking up for other students that became the rep work of Chapter 06.
m.c:now: A snapshot with a date on it, so the record stays honest: finished work moves into its chapter, and each update rebuilds this page from the record.
m.e:education_life-tju-self-improvement-aw: Received Tianjin University’s Beiyang Self-Improvement Award in 2021, as the degree began — a small badge at the very start of the walk.
m.e:education_life-tju-bsc-enrol: Joined the School of Mathematics at Tianjin University in 2021, in a mathematics honours class, and read Mathematics and Applied Mathematics until June 2025. Courses included mathematical analysis, advanced algebra, real and complex analysis, and mathematical modelling. Qualified for exemption from the national postgraduate entrance exam.
m.e:education_life-tju-rowing: Rowed for the Tianjin University rowing team from September 2021 to June 2023, taking second place in the mixed 2000 m at the 4th Tianjin Water Sports Games and cutting a personal 500 m time by about fifteen per cent over the two years. A physical rhythm under the mathematics: stroke, recover, repeat.
m.e:projects_code-github-identity: The GitHub account dates from 1 December 2021. For three years it was quiet — coursework, a maths guide, a template — and then, in 2026, it erupted: most of the repositories were created that year, along with nearly all of the contributions, including a two-day spike when automated coding agents built a hackathon product. The counts on this page come from GitHub’s public contribution calendar, up to the last day shown under it. Company work in private repositories is not counted, so the graph is a lower bound, not the whole output.
m.e:education_life-tju-first-year-essays: Two end-of-term essays for the first-year special-topic courses in analysis and algebra, both dated 24 December 2021: ‘Darboux’s theorem’, seven pages on why a derivative cannot jump, and ‘Hilbert’s third problem’, fifteen pages on whether any two polyhedra of equal volume can be cut into matching pieces. The first long-form mathematics.
m.e:education_life-nsca-cpt: Earned the NSCA Certified Personal Trainer credential in the winter of 2022, out of an interest in training and fitness. It is an unexpected line on a mathematician’s record — and perhaps why the lunch-optimisation post treats complete nutrition as a hard constraint.
m.e:education_life-tju-outstanding-cadre: Named an Outstanding Student Leader of Tianjin University in 2022, for the student-leadership work of the first two years — the thread of service that later reappears in Bristol as a PGR representative.
m.e:education_life-tju-freshmen-guide: Led a team of three class guides supporting more than a hundred incoming mathematics students through August and September 2022 — campus tours, answering questions, and acting as the link between new students and staff. A year later, the same instinct produced the maths guide.
m.e:education_life-tju-student-union-right: Led the Rights and Welfare department of the Tianjin University School of Mathematics student union from September 2022 to June 2023, resolving more than forty student issues on dormitories and facilities and organising more than twenty dialogues between students and the university. It was the first time representing other students — and the role came back, three years later, in Bristol.
m.e:education_life-bristol-3plus1-pathway: The degree’s last stage ran through the 3+1 route between Tianjin University and the University of Bristol: three years at Tianjin (the third on exchange in Hong Kong), then a one-year MSc at Bristol. Selection came in November 2022; the move was made in September 2024. Because the bachelor’s (to June 2025) and the master’s (from September 2024) overlap, Fig. 11 draws this as a shortcut: the line reaches Bristol a year earlier than it otherwise would.
m.e:us_ai_internship_career-light-painting: In May 2023 a portfolio of light-painting photographs came together: long exposures in which a moving light draws paths that accumulate on the sensor over several seconds. It is the direct ancestor of this site’s central image — a dark plate on which the paths of thousands of walkers accumulate into light.
m.e:projects_code-tju-math-guide: Rather than just taking the courses, I wrote a guide to them for the students who come after. Started in July 2023, the Tianjin University maths undergraduate guide gathers what a student needs — a foreword, the core courses, the degree programmes and how to contribute — first as a quick guide with a document library, then as a MkDocs site. It has been served at zhouyixiaoxiao.info since December 2025 and is the oldest thing on this page, still online.
m.e:gap_1_linkedin_full_profile-account-an: LinkedIn’s email footers keep a quiet record of the profile’s one-line headline: ‘student in Tianjin University’ in July 2023; a day later, ‘Applied Math Student @Tianjin University // Transforming Complexity into Simplicity’; then the same with a line seeking UK summer internships; then back to the plain applied-maths student; and from 20 September 2024, ‘Engineering Mathematics Student @University of Bristol’. That last one has not changed since — not for the PhD, the fellowship or the company role. This site is, in part, the overdue headline update.
m.e:projects_code-tju-draw: A Windows drawing application written in C++ with MFC for the Tianjin University School of Mathematics computer practicum: draw lines, circles, ellipses, squares, rectangles and triangles, change stroke and fill colours, then drag, scale and rotate the shapes to any angle. The earliest interactive graphics in this collection — the plate on the home page is a distant descendant.
m.e:education_life-hkust-booth-promoter: While on exchange, ran an information booth representing Tianjin University at HKUST, telling visiting students in English and Chinese about research, collaboration and exchange opportunities — an ambassador before the title existed.
m.e:education_life-hkust-exchange: Spent the 2023–24 academic year as an exchange student at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, taking partial differential equations, numerical solution of PDEs and applied statistics. It was where the mathematics turned computational — and where a first neural-network research project began.
m.e:self_media-camera-roll-corpus: An inventory of the personal camera roll in August 2026 counted 3,947 videos shot between 3 September 2023 and 27 August 2026 — 140 in 2023, 1,310 in 2024, 1,574 in 2025 and 923 in 2026 up to August. Month by month, the counts show quiet stretches and clear peaks. Only these aggregates are published; the clips themselves stay private.
m.e:education_life-hkust-pinns-report: A research project at HKUST from November 2023 to May 2024 used physics-informed neural networks in PyTorch to solve partial differential equations — one-dimensional diffusion, a two-dimensional wave equation and Laplace’s equation in two and three dimensions — comparing uniform and random sampling of the training points. The 22-page report, ‘Using PINN to solve diffusion, wave and Laplace equations’, is dated 31 May 2024. It is the earliest point on the thread from mathematics to AI.
m.e:education_life-chengdu-expo-media-spee: During the summer internship programme of 2024, a visit to the Chengdu World Horticultural Expo on 23 July ended up in a local news report that quoted by name. Around it came speeches at the opening and closing ceremonies of the summer programme for university students — a first stage, and a first microphone.
m.e:us_ai_internship_career-jll-chengdu-in: A research internship in the Chengdu research department of JLL (Jones Lang LaSalle, a global real-estate consultancy) in the summer of 2024, through the Sichuan–Hong Kong summer internship programme, joined while on exchange at HKUST: data-driven market research, collecting and cleaning large retail datasets in Python, and turning them into findings for stakeholders. The programme’s visits — Guang’an, the Sanxingdui Museum, the panda base — made it a month of Sichuan as well as spreadsheets.
m.e:education_life-bristol-msc-start: Moved to Bristol in September 2024 for the MSc in Engineering Mathematics. Modules included statistical computing and empirical methods; information theory and coding; renewable energy; mathematical modelling in biology, medicine and public health; methods of AI; and skills in mathematical research. It finished with a Distinction and a dissertation on first-passage times of random walks in confined spaces: how long a walker takes to first reach its target (Chapter 01).
m.e:education_life-student-warden: During the MSc year, worked part-time as a Student Warden in Bristol student accommodation: duty shifts giving residents frontline support and responding to fire alarms under the safety procedures, with fire-warden training completed in December 2024.
m.e:research_fpt-msc-dissertation: The MSc in Engineering Mathematics at Bristol (2024–25) finished with a Distinction (the top UK grade) and a dissertation titled ‘First-Passage Phenomena in Confined Random Walks: Finite-Size Effects, Exact Solutions, and Spatial Heterogeneity’. It asked how long a random walker takes to first reach a target on one-, two- and three-dimensional lattices, with and without defects, and set exact solutions against simulation. The code is public. It is the first place the walker got trapped in a box — and the question has not let go since.
m.e:self_media-linkedin-impressions-series: Until this site, LinkedIn was the de facto public page: the QR codes on the enterprise poster and on the ambassador posters point there. Its posts mark the milestones — starting the PhD, the enterprise fellowship, the festival pitch — with the odd lighter one, such as lunch treated as an optimisation problem.
m.e:gap_1_linkedin_full_profile-post-perso: On 3 October 2024 a LinkedIn post announced a first personal website, built a few months after the Tianjin maths guide. Its launch essay was a small personal credo: real freedom exists within constraints, and a game is most fun just beyond your comfort zone. Read again now, it describes a random walker in a bounded box. The address you are reading spent most of 2026 as a redirect to LinkedIn; this site is the third attempt.
m.e:projects_code-tju-letter-template: A bilingual XeLaTeX template that reproduces Tianjin University’s letterhead style — TJU blue, a logo slot, a contact block — written during the PhD application season for reference letters, then published so that anyone else applying could use it too. It was announced on LinkedIn twenty-five minutes after the repository was created.
m.e:education_life-causal-logistics-projec: In a five-person MSc team project with an industry partner in logistics, led the synthesis of more than fifteen causal-inference papers and applied structural causal models to an aviation dataset of about 29,000 points, isolating the effect of weather on delays while controlling for latitude and season. The team combined the causal analysis with Kolmogorov–Arnold networks.
m.e:education_life-geneva-un-field-exchang: A winter study programme in Geneva built around the UN Office at Geneva, 8–17 February 2025 — the Youth Training Program at the UN run by the World Federation of United Nations Associations (WFUNA), with workshops on humanitarian affairs, multilateralism, diplomacy and the Sustainable Development Goals. In a thirty-person mock UN conference, represented Australia and led the drafting of a fifteen-minute script for a vaccine-cooperation conference; the group visited six international organisations: WIPO, the ILO, the FAO, UNODA, CERN and the IFRC.
m.e:gap_1_linkedin_full_profile-su-student: Stood for Student Trustee in the Bristol Students’ Union elections in February–March 2025 as a self-nominated MSc candidate, and campaigned through voting week — announcing the run publicly on LinkedIn. More than 7,700 students voted in that term’s elections. It was the first time standing for anything at Bristol, nine months before becoming a PhD representative.
m.e:education_life-languages: Mandarin Chinese is native, English is the working language and French is at A1. In practice the working life is bilingual by default: talks, papers, documentation and websites — this one included — usually ship in English and Chinese at once, and one research paper is about what happens when people type to AI in the space between the two.
m.e:education_life-tju-undergrad-thesis: The Tianjin University undergraduate thesis, completed in May 2025, couples lattice random walks with SIR epidemic dynamics to model disease spread in heterogeneous indoor spaces. The 2026 article developed from it proves bounds on the reproduction number, simulates four indoor scenes exactly (office, supermarket, classroom, metro carriage) and confronts the model, under pre-specified protocols, with 38 documented outbreaks, contact records and tracer measurements, reporting where it fails. The random walk was already there before the PhD.
m.e:education_life-tju-graduation: Completed the Tianjin University BSc in Mathematics and Applied Mathematics in June 2025, while already in the final months of the Bristol MSc through the joint route — two degree bars closing within three months of each other.
m.e:education_life-hkust-engineering-summe: Selected for the 2025 Summer Camp for Elite Students (21–25 July) at the School of Engineering of the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST), a camp for prospective research postgraduates that included a visit to the Hong Kong Science Park. The first days in Hong Kong led straight on to the Bay Area — the opening of a three-city summer: Hong Kong, Silicon Valley, Bristol.
m.e:us_ai_internship_career-silicon-valley: About three weeks in the Bay Area on Tianjin University’s Silicon Valley Entrepreneurship Program — a ‘Stanford & Silicon Valley’ programme run with Founders Space, a San Francisco venture builder, for a cohort of about twenty students. I came straight from the Hong Kong camp, and the weeks filled up with a design-thinking workshop, visits to Silicon Valley companies, a symposium at Stanford and evening founder-and-investor meetups — and, inside the same window, a research internship at LiveX AI.
m.e:us_ai_internship_career-aasf-pioneer-m: The first weekend after landing in San Francisco meant a student ticket for the Saturday session of the Asian American Scholar Forum’s Pioneer Medal Symposium and Ceremony at Stanford Memorial Auditorium, 26 July 2025 — the opening frame of the whole Bay Area chapter.
m.e:gap_3_us_internship_origin-group3-gett: In the first week on site the cohort took a Stanford-style design-thinking workshop, with the worked example ‘new students feel lost at Stanford’. Group 3’s bilingual write-up turned getting lost into a feature: every wrong turn lights a community beacon and reveals a hidden story. It proposed four ‘bridges’ — E-ink beacon tags for leaving notes, a story-card deck whose AR clues unlock only on site, a sculpture projecting a live heat-map of wandering, and Bluetooth guide beacons carried by senior students — and scored wandering paths as ‘Bravery Points’. A random walk rewarded for wandering: the idea turns up again on this site.
m.e:us_ai_internship_career-livex-ai-inter: LiveX AI, a Bay Area AI start-up, helps consumer companies use AI for customer support, retention and growth. The work ran from a survey of document parsers and a six-dimension quality rubric to a vendor compliance matrix for the engineering team, and ended in a benchmark that checks whether each parser’s output can actually answer questions.
m.e:gap_3_us_internship_origin-reflection-: About a week into the programme came a six-part Chinese reflection of roughly 1,700 characters: a night arrival; the Pacific coast and a quiet Stanford campus; walking into the campuses of the big technology companies; conversations with investors and founders; and dawn over the Alviso salt flats. It ends on motivation — everyone stands on a different rung of a ladder wrapped in cloud, so just take your own next step.
m.e:us_ai_internship_career-livex-tool-sur: The first week was a sprint: an investigation note on parsing benchmarks and popular tools, four converters run over nine representative test PDFs the same evening, and a written comparison the next day. When the engineering team asked for numbers and one more tool, a fifth was added, and by the end of the week a first deck scored the leading options from 0 to 10 on six dimensions — structural fidelity, formatting accuracy, special content, cleanliness, ease of post-processing and automation readiness. A follow-up request for something runnable set up the benchmark of week two.
m.e:us_ai_internship_career-livex-retrieva: The internship’s study became a benchmark in its final week, once the engineering team asked for something it could run. The question behind it: which parser turns product manuals into text an AI assistant can reliably answer questions from? Each parser’s output (plain-text Markdown) is treated as a knowledge base and judged by downstream usefulness rather than visual fidelity: the text is split into passages, the most relevant ones are found, and a model answers only from those passages — it may say ‘not found’. Every answer is scored first by checking for the exact answer, then by a grader following a written scoring guide. Wrong answers given with confidence are tracked separately as overconfidence. Five parsers, nine documents, a hundred questions per document: 900 questions for every parser.
m.e:education_life-msc-distinction: The MSc in Engineering Mathematics at the University of Bristol was awarded with Distinction in 2025. Two months later the same school became the home of the PhD — the walker stayed in the box, and went deeper.
m.e:gap_1_linkedin_full_profile-position-l: The summer’s question returns in ime-eval and in a first-author paper accepted as a poster at UKAIRS, the UK AI Research Symposium (Chapter 02). Four months after the summer came BioPath and the enterprise fellowship (Chapter 07); in June 2026 applied AI became a job — R&D Scientist (AI) at Yuexin International, a cloud-communications company (Chapter 03).
m.e:gap_1_linkedin_full_profile-post-food-: A LinkedIn post set out a ‘food philosophy, PhD edition’ as an optimisation problem: stay reliably fed without leaving the office too often. Two objectives — speed (under fifteen minutes a meal, often under ten, because other work runs in parallel while a potato is in the microwave) and cost — and one hard constraint: nutrition must be complete, macro and micro. It is a joke, and it is also exactly how everything else on this site gets decided.
m.e:education_life-phd-start: The PhD began on 3 November 2025 in the School of Engineering Mathematics and Technology (SEMT) at the University of Bristol. The subject is first-passage time: how long a random walker takes to reach a target for the first time, and why the distribution of that time can split into two peaks. The work has since broadened to span stochastic processes and the evaluation of AI agents. The random walks moving across this page are the same kind of object the thesis studies.
m.e:school_teaching_service-tsr-contracts-: Within weeks of starting the PhD, signed up to teach and took on two contracts: a Demonstrator role in the School of Engineering Mathematics and Technology in early December 2025, and a Graduate Teacher role in the School of Mathematics for the teaching block starting in January 2026. From then on, teaching ran alongside the PhD: problem classes, labs and marking.
m.e:self_media-linkedin-phd-post: On 21 November 2025 a one-line LinkedIn post shared the news: ‘I’m happy to share that I’m starting a new position as PHD Student at University of Bristol!’ — and the profile photo changed the same evening. A small post for a long walk: the PhD it announced is Chapter 01.
m.e:research_fpt-rw-defects-prototype: Within four weeks of starting, a first prototype was specified and built: a Python simulation of a random walk on a one-dimensional ring with defects, with analysis scripts, parameter scans and a small web visualiser. One configuration already hinted at a two-humped first-passage histogram. It was a sketch rather than a result, and it was archived once the exact methods arrived — but it is the baby picture of the whole research line.
m.e:school_teaching_service-semt-pgr-rep-2: Stepped forward on 1 December 2025; after the Students’ Union’s rep and communication training, the role was confirmed in January 2026. Through the year’s school and faculty rep forums, PhD students’ points were carried upward — in person, through the co-rep or online — and the careers service agreed to add a general careers Q&A to a PhD lunch-and-learn.
m.e:research_fpt-isambard-hpc: From December 2025 the heavy computation ran on Isambard, the UK national AI supercomputers hosted in Bristol, as part of a university project on random walkers in disordered environments. Command-line automation syncs the code, submits jobs to the scheduler and fetches the results. Isambard-AI carried the encounter paper’s heavy runs from the lattice to the continuum limit — lattice ladders refined up to n = 33 and Brownian dynamics with 20 million walkers per release position — and Isambard 3 ran the large-scale checks for the fixed-budget paper in September 2026, including a census of 2 billion walkers.
m.e:research_fpt-jumpover-ring-reports: The ring studies were consolidated into bilingual reports: a lazy ring with a one-way shortcut, two neighbour kernels, scans over shortcut strength β and ring size N, Monte Carlo trajectory classes and tail diagnostics. The long-time tail turned out to be set by the spectral radius of the transient chain, and β* = 0.01 was the smallest shortcut strength at which both kernels meet the double-peak criterion. A suspicious plateau in one figure was traced to a truncation in the numerical inversion and fixed — the first of many bugs caught by refusing to trust a pretty curve.
m.e:school_teaching_service-ecef-awarded: The application, on 11 December 2025, proposed turning first-passage research into trap-placement software. On 23 December it won one of twelve places in the University of Bristol’s 2026 Early Career Enterprise Fellowship.
m.e:research_fpt-grid2d-family: In 2026 the question moved from rings to two-dimensional lattices — periodic, rectangular and reflecting domains, a membrane near the target, two competing targets, local bias fields and two-walker encounters. Of the 27 reports in the public research atlas, 13 belong to this lattice family. One finding: a membrane’s permeability mainly adds to the time spent after the crossing, which is why some geometries keep a clear double peak even with minimal bias.
m.e:school_teaching_service-financial-math: From January to May 2026, taught problem classes for the third-year and MSc unit Financial Mathematics in the School of Mathematics, and marked its formative and then its assessed problem sheets — including getting marks and written feedback back to students through the virtual learning environment in bulk rather than one by one.
m.e:gap_5_school_teams_gmail_coauthor-rep-: The first post as rep in the SEMT PhD community, on 5 January 2026, opened with a pronunciation guide — Xiaoxiao is ‘SHYOW-shyow’ — then a line about the research (random walks on lattices, first-passage problems) and an invitation to send feedback to the School. Later posts passed along opportunities: a translational funding call, a study group with industry, and volunteers for the faculty’s PhD induction panel.
m.e:school_teaching_service-mdm3-2026-tb2: Supported third-year modelling teams in Mathematical and Data Modelling 3 during the second teaching block, including a group working on an industry-set project: structured written feedback on their report, help re-laying it in the university’s LaTeX template, and peer-evaluation input as the group’s teaching-support lead. Along the way, a small copy-ready web tool made delivering blocks of feedback faster.
m.e:school_teaching_service-pgr-feedback-f: Built a standing anonymous feedback form for SEMT PhD students with the fellow rep; the School circulated it to every Engineering Mathematics PhD student on 19 January 2026. Then typeset matching posters in TikZ and LaTeX in a teal house style: a QR poster headed ‘Make your PhD better.’ and a notice about evening building works in the PhD rooms. The same visual language later carried over to the ambassador posters.
m.e:school_teaching_service-ai-native-teac: Behind the teaching sits a workflow: all teaching-support material organised into a structured course hub with an index written for AI agents, and agents that rebuilt a whole term’s allocations, timetable clashes and weekly plans from mail records, calendars and shared rotas. It is the same method as the research — structure first, then let agents do the tedious reconstruction, then check it — applied to a whole year of teaching.
m.e:school_teaching_service-data-science-t: Marked a batch of first-theme coursework for the MSc unit Data Science Methods and Practice in the School of Engineering Mathematics and Technology in February 2026, working from the theme brief and a shared marking sheet so that every script was judged against the same criteria.
m.e:self_media-linkedin-ecef-post: A LinkedIn post in February 2026 announced the appointment as a University of Bristol Early Career Enterprise Fellow for 2026, describing the PhD research on random walks and first-passage phenomena on graphs, and how it can inform decisions under uncertainty — the same mathematics that became BioPath.
m.e:school_teaching_service-emat20013-lab-: Invited in February 2026 to test, sort and inspect the lab kits used by undergraduates in Principles of Physical Modelling: two on-site testing days and an inspection report with photographic evidence of every defect. A hands-on counterpoint to the theory — a mathematician debugging physical kit.
m.e:visual_assets-ink-wash-art: Two vertical images made with AI image generation under close art direction: a Chinese ink-wash landscape with a red sun, a pagoda, cranes, deer and a lone boat, made as a red-envelope cover in February 2026, and a remix with red lanterns and a gate for the Lunar New Year. Monochrome ink and a single vermilion accent — the palette this site is built on.
m.e:ai_research-openclaw-agent-host: A spare laptop became an always-on host for an open-source autonomous agent framework, driven from a phone through ordinary chat apps to run coding and browser tasks, with multi-agent channels, scheduled digests and an automated development loop for the SocialOS codebase. About two months of real use surfaced where autonomous agents break today: authentication churn, reliability when nobody is watching, and permissions that sprawl. The whole setup was uninstalled in July 2026 — the experiment was the point.
m.e:school_teaching_service-ecef-training-: The fellowship came with a training programme run with the university’s enterprise partner — building a team, funding and investment — and two rounds of PechaKucha coaching, in May online and in June in person, ahead of the Festival of Enterprise. PechaKucha is unforgiving: twenty slides, twenty seconds each, no going back.
m.e:projects_code-biopath-platform: The software behind the fellowship: a Python platform with a command-line tool, an API and a static site with a demo that runs in the browser. It takes a site map and a monitoring budget and returns trap or sensor coordinates chosen so that a wandering pest is as likely as possible to be caught within a set time, together with an evidence bundle anyone can re-run (the repository calls it the proof bundle) — the optimised score against heuristic and random baselines, the worst-case score across stress-test scenarios and the Monte Carlo runs behind them. The maps in the repository are synthetic demos, and the project site is live.
m.e:research_fpt-ai-native-research-method: Across the first-passage line a repeatable loop took shape: AI models propose derivations and code, separate agents attack the claims, numerical computation acts as the arbiter, and exact algebra is machine-checked in Lean 4, a proof assistant. The documented cases include proposed formulas that failed numerical checks and were discarded, a repository-grounded audit that caught errors an outside model could not see, and multi-round reviews — up to about sixty agents in a single audit — before each submission. The principle in one line: AI can generate more scientific possibilities; the research skill is deciding which ones deserve belief.
m.e:research_fpt-research-atlas: On 25–26 February 2026 the first-passage line got its own public website: a static research atlas in English and Chinese, with a continuous ‘book’ of eight chapters, a page for every report, a theory section, interactive figures and typeset mathematics. It maps 27 reports and tracks 130 claims back to their evidence. The repository behind it is organised ‘agent-first’ — one command-line tool, guardrail tests and a machine-readable report registry — so that people and AI agents can work on it in the same way.
m.e:self_media-ei-blog-ecef-feature: The university’s Enterprise & Innovation blog introduced the 2026 cohort of Early Career Enterprise Fellows on 26 February 2026, including a statement on BioPath: a software tool for more precise and sustainable pest management on farms and grain-storage sites, aiming to cut reliance on chemical rodenticides. The post was also featured in that day’s bulletin.
m.e:ai_research-uk-ai-agent-hack-socialos: Took part in the week-long UK AI Agent Hackathon EP4, which opened on 1 March 2026 at Imperial College London — and shared the call with the PhD community of SEMT, the School of Engineering Mathematics and Technology the day before. The entry was SocialOS, submitted to five bounty tracks at once; the public repository keeps the pitch pack, the architecture and the evidence documents.
m.e:school_teaching_service-new-enterprise: Accepted onto New Enterprise’s Development stage, run by the Careers Service, in January 2026; then weekly workshops, a pitch on 24 February in the Wills Memorial Building, and a £150 award for BioPath on 2 March 2026 — a small first win on the road from theorem to product.
m.e:projects_code-socialos: SocialOS turns raw notes, voice memos, screenshots and encounters into structured memory about people and events, reflections on yourself and drafts for each platform, delivered through a publishing queue that a human approves. It runs only on the local machine. It was built for the UK AI Agent Hack in five days, with 1,222 commits between 5 and 9 March 2026 — 1,084 of them tagged ‘[autodev]’: commits made by the automated coding agents set up for that week. The public repository keeps the pitch pack and the evidence.
m.e:school_teaching_service-new-enterprise: After the development award, BioPath moved on to the Growth stage of New Enterprise, in its 2025/26 cohort — a series of masterclasses through the spring and a mentor from the university’s research and commercialisation team, matched in late March 2026.
m.e:ai_research-agent-skills-oss: A public, sanitised collection of reusable skills and setup kits for coding agents — mail access, security-minded skills and a portable configuration template — plus small utilities for AI desktop apps. The larger personal library stays private; what is published is what anyone can safely reuse.
m.e:company_products-sms-classifier: An on-device classifier for Chinese SMS, built for a cloud-communications company: a large language model acted as the teacher, labelling examples, and its judgement was distilled into a lightweight student that sorts each message into verification codes, notifications or marketing in well under a millisecond. Three student models were compared on a labelled test set; a support-vector machine (a classic, lightweight classifier) won, with a macro-F1 of 0.91 (an average score that weights every category equally). Fraud detection was deliberately left out of scope.
m.e:projects_code-atlas-voice-fix: A bilingual repository that diagnosed why voice input failed in the ChatGPT Atlas browser — it stored its own audio-input priority and preferred an external monitor’s microphone over the built-in one — and ships an audit script and a reversible fix that reorders the priority, plus a userscript that keeps video speed controls on ordinary sites.
m.e:gap_5_school_teams_gmail_coauthor-idea: As one of the two SEMT PGR reps, joined the organising group for SEMT Ideas Exchange Week from March 2026, alongside the PhD programme leads and postdoc and staff representatives. The week settled into two showcase days — PhD research on 15 April and postdoctoral research on 17 April — and the Hidden Routes talk was scheduled for the same week.
m.e:research_fpt-bamc-2026: Attended the British Applied Mathematics Colloquium 2026 at the University of East Anglia in Norwich, which opened on 30 March 2026 — the first national applied-mathematics meeting of the PhD, and a first look at where first-passage questions sit within the wider field.
m.e:education_life-iceland-ring-road-2026: In April 2026, a self-drive around Iceland’s ring road, along the south coast and through the East Fjords to Akureyri, with a stop in Oslo. For one snowy leg — Bakkagerði to Akureyri by Route 94, Mývatn, Húsavík and Goðafoss — a public Chinese route-decision site laid out A, B and C options with links to the official road conditions. Planning a trip like a product, again.
m.e:research_fpt-hidden-routes-talk: A ten-minute talk for PhD students across SEMT, the School of Engineering Mathematics and Technology, given at its Ideas Exchange Day and built as a web slide deck inside the research atlas, with a live random-walk animation and figures regenerated from the research code. Its one-line thesis: a single target on a ring still produces a fast branch, a valley and a delayed branch once one directed shortcut is present. Deck and script are public in both languages.
m.e:school_teaching_service-student-ambass: Signed on as a University of Bristol Student Ambassador in April 2026 and worked the undergraduate open days on 12–13 June — wearing a home-designed ‘Ask me about…’ poster for Engineering Maths and AI.
m.e:ai_research-global-hacktour-london: At the in-person Global HackTour London at UCL on 18–19 April 2026, built ‘London Cuts — One City, Three Cuts’: upload a London memory and get back a story in three narrative modes — Punk, Fashion, Cinema — along with a collectible postcard and a pin on a story atlas. The weekend prototype became the London Cuts product.
m.e:projects_code-london-cuts: A creator tool for a single-place trip: photos placed by their own metadata, written stories and AI-generated postcards in six art styles, with public reader pages in three visual modes (Punk, Fashion, Cinema), a map atlas and PDF or PNG export. The live demo tells ‘A Year Around London’ in thirteen stops and ‘A Week in Reykjavík’, and it has entry points for AI agents too: an llms.txt, an OpenAPI description and an MCP endpoint (MCP is an open protocol that lets AI call outside tools). London Cuts is a working name.
m.e:projects_code-bristol-housing-map: A single-page map for incoming Chinese Master of Laws (LLM) students at Bristol: seventeen student housing options within about a twenty-minute walk of the Law School, each tagged by how its information was sourced — verified, provider, search or live — with an application section, a mobile detail panel and an offline basemap fallback. Built in a weekend, with an editorial look borrowed from fashion magazines.
m.e:ai_research-direction-toward-ai: Alongside first-passage research on random walks, the PhD work broadened during 2026 toward AI: evaluating AI agents built on large language models (first, whether they can be instructed in pinyin alone), and using multi-model AI workflows as research instruments — adversarial audits whose disagreements are settled by computation. The habit carries straight over: measure the hidden route, then refuse to believe the number until something independent confirms it. The UKAIRS 2026 acceptance is its first peer-reviewed AI output.
m.e:school_teaching_service-somerscience-2: Helped run the University of Bristol Engineering Mathematics stand at the Somerscience family science festival at the Bath & West Showground on 4 May 2026, with hands-on exhibits for children and families — a double pendulum, a swarm-robot jigsaw and interactive pieces from Bristol’s science centre — and drove fellow volunteers to the site.
m.e:gap_4_event_attendance_calendar-gosim-: Attended GOSIM Paris 2026, ‘The Agentic AI Convergence’, at Station F, the Paris start-up campus, on 5–6 May. The takeaway, written up afterwards: open-source agent ecosystems are moving away from model showcases toward tool interoperability, model serving, edge deployment, production systems and trustworthy workflows — the same direction the evaluation work was heading.
m.e:school_teaching_service-sparck-ai-scho: Served on a twelve-member Faculty of Science and Engineering panel reviewing applications for the Spärck AI Scholarships at Bristol in May and June 2026: after a training session, each application was scored against a shared marking scheme, and shortlisting results went to applicants on 10 June, ahead of interviews. It was a view of AI talent from the selection side.
m.e:company_design_events-ai-skill-guide: A 13-page Chinese guide for anyone new to AI agents, on when and how to turn a successful agent session into a reusable skill file: a decision framework, an operating procedure, a template, two worked examples and a one-page checklist. Its argument in one line: a skill is not a longer prompt — it is a reusable instruction manual for the AI.
m.e:company_products-agent-comms-thesis: In May 2026, in a series of memos and one-pagers, an argument took shape: communication becomes the execution layer for AI agents. An agent that can reach people through the channels they already use — messages, notifications — is an agent that can finish a job. It is a personal thesis rather than company strategy, and it explains why a first-passage mathematician ended up building AI systems inside a cloud-communications company whose core business is SMS.
m.e:ai_research-ime-eval-scaffold: ime-eval is the instrument behind the study. It drives real command-line coding agents rather than raw APIs, pairs every native-script prompt with keyboard-friendly variants — clean pinyin, no spaces, light typos, initials, and mixed prompts that keep key terms in native script — and defines profiles for eight input styles, from Japanese romaji and Vietnamese with few or no diacritics to Hinglish, Arabizi, Russian transliteration, Greeklish and Korean. Hard rules from day one: configurations generated automatically, dry-run by default, results written once, and sandboxes that keep answers from leaking to the agent. Named here, not yet public.
m.e:ai_research-three-agent-relay: The study ran as a relay between AI systems. An orchestrating model wrote each phase brief; a coding agent implemented and ran it; a third, independent agent audited readiness before any real call was spent — for the homophone phase it returned ‘safe to run’. Every phase ended with a state-and-decision packet handed back to the orchestrator, and every step was committed to git. The human role was the architect’s: choose the phases, authorise the spend, carry the baton.
m.e:research_fpt-multitimescale-brief: A 12-page brief pulled the year’s cases together — ring shortcuts, two-target lattices and exact two-walker encounter searches — and argued that a visible double peak needs three things at once: a balance between the masses of the fast and slow channels, well-separated timescales, and a valley deep enough to resolve. A second talk page on multi-timescale encounters, with a live two-dimensional hopping demo, joined the atlas on 31 May 2026.
m.e:ai_research-ime-eval-first-real-call: Before any model call was spent, the harness was hardened: leakage-neutral work directories, an environment-gated switch for real runs with a hard cap on calls, preflight checks and deterministic scoring, each reviewed by an independent audit. The first real smoke test took four authorised calls and exposed four invocation bugs — relative schema paths, a blocked input stream and the strict rules of structured output. Once they were fixed, the pipeline answered correctly and scored 1.0. The test suite grew from 47 to 87 along the way.
m.e:projects_code-catchmouse: A clean Swift rewrite of CatchMouse, an Intel-only utility from 2011: a menu-bar agent that warps the cursor to the left, centre or right display with global hotkeys, cycles between displays, remembers custom hotkeys per monitor, flashes display numbers and offers command-line verbs. It builds a universal app with only the command-line tools and needs no accessibility permission. MIT-licensed.
m.e:ai_research-condition-distinctness-fix: A zero-cost audit of all 24 pilot tasks found that the ‘abbreviation’ condition produced prompts byte-for-byte identical to clean romanisation on three tasks — one Chinese, two Vietnamese — which would have silently wasted real calls. A deterministic, script-aware transform now renders syllable initials for Chinese, Japanese and Korean (so ‘shang dian li’ becomes ‘sdl’), and the variant lock records a digest of every rendered prompt, so that even a code-only change is caught by drift checks.
m.e:ai_research-phase2-curves: An arithmetic task came back correct under all six input shapes — good evidence that the plumbing worked, but a saturated test. A constraint-following task discriminated: clean pinyin, pinyin without spaces, pinyin with typos and a mixed prompt with English technical terms all returned the required three-item JSON array (a list format a program can read directly), while pinyin initials recovered the topic but lost the structure and scored 0.333. Under a placeholder keystroke model the initials needed an estimated 0.39 of the native keystrokes: a large estimated saving, and a measured loss in quality.
m.e:ai_research-phase3-normalize-backfires: A small twelve-call repetition reproduced the lower score for abbreviations: direct answers to pinyin-initial prompts averaged 0.444 against 1.0 for native prompts. A ‘normalise, then answer’ wrapper did not rescue it. The mean fell to 0.333 because the model judged the initials too lossy and declined to answer in all three repetitions — turning confident wrong output into honest abstention. Native prompts were unaffected. It is a negative result, and it stayed in the paper.
m.e:ai_research-phase4-homophone: Three adversarial tasks hinge on words that collapse without tones: shu alone is 书 ‘book’, 树 ‘tree’, 输 ‘lose’ and 熟 ‘ripe’. In this exploratory test, native characters scored 1.00, and so did the mixed workflow — instructions in pinyin, critical terms in characters. Clean, unspaced and misspelt pinyin all averaged 0.333: the agent left the answer in pinyin or picked the wrong character. The one task that survived, 买 ‘buy’ against 卖 ‘sell’, was saved by 入 ‘in’ and 出 ‘out’. An uncalibrated estimate puts the mixed prompt at 0.82 of the input-method keystrokes; typing effort was not measured.
m.e:company_products-joined-yuexin: Joined Yuexin International (brand: Yuexin Cloud) in June 2026, alongside the PhD; the company’s business spans messaging, voice and AI. Besides the systems below, the work has included drafting the company’s AI plan in July and serving as lead trainer and technical judge for the operations team’s agent training.
m.e:self_media-festival-pitch-video: That same night the Festival of Enterprise pitch and its Q&A were edited into an 8 min 58 s video with 135 burned-in Chinese–English subtitle cues, transcribed by two speech models and corrected line by line against the script. It is published on WeChat Channels, the short-video feed inside WeChat, under the name 周易潇潇 (Zhouyi Xiaoxiao), with a Chinese title that reads ‘Bristol enterprise festival talk’ — search for it in WeChat to watch.
m.e:company_products-feishu-agent-connecto: A suite of MCP connectors (MCP is an open protocol that lets AI call outside tools) that lets coding agents work inside the company’s workspace in Feishu (also known as Lark, a workplace chat-and-docs suite) — documents, sheets, chats, meeting minutes and approvals — with scoped permissions, acting as the signed-in person rather than as an all-powerful bot. Written documentation made it something colleagues could install, not just a demo.
m.e:school_teaching_service-lighter-side-o: ‘The Lighter Side of Research’, run by the doctoral colleges of Bath, Bristol and Bath Spa, trains PhD researchers to turn their research into stand-up. After three workshops in Bath and Bristol through the spring, the programme’s first public show took place on 3 June 2026 at The Mount Without in Bristol, and the set — about seven minutes on doing a maths PhD — ran in the first half.
m.e:school_teaching_service-writers-retrea: At the School PhD director’s request, drafted and circulated a short interest check on structured writing retreats for SEMT PhD students. Every one of the seven respondents said yes; the School confirmed two retreat sessions of forty places each, and they were advertised to PhD students for July 2026. A tiny data story with a tangible result.
m.e:ai_research-claude-cross-check: Nine real calls to Claude Code on the same three homophone tasks reproduced the pattern exactly: native and mixed prompts scored 1.00, clean pinyin averaged 0.333. The pinyin ‘shi shi jian yan’, for example, came back as 实时检验 (‘real-time check’) for both items, instead of 事实检验 (‘fact check’) and 实施检验 (‘implementation check’). Two earlier batches were excluded as infrastructure failures rather than counted. The check made the finding cross-agent — reported in the paper as a small check, not a model comparison.
m.e:ai_research-phase5-model-drift: A prepared 48-call boundary study, with a new glossary condition, returned an error on every call. For reproducibility the harness ignored the command-line tool’s user configuration, so it fell back to a built-in default model that the signed-in account could not use. The batch was reported as a failure rather than scored as data; the model was then pinned explicitly and a one-call smoke confirmed the fix. The audit trail surfaced a second lesson: the exact model behind the earlier successful phases had not been recorded. Product tools change underneath you — pin exact model IDs.
m.e:ai_research-ukairs-submission: ‘Skipping the IME? Keyboard-Friendly Multilingual Prompting for LLM Agents’ went to UKAIRS 2026, the UK AI Research Symposium, on 8 June: a two-page paper in the Emerging Research track, under the theme of synergistic human–AI collaboration, typeset so that the Chinese examples render inside an ACM template. It reports 48 valid text-only zh-CN calls — 39 to Codex and 9 to Claude Code, two AI coding agents — and proposes a design rule: skipping the IME (the input method) may be fine for routine scaffolding, but exact names, domain terms and homophones need native-script anchoring. Authors: Xiaoxiao Zhouyi and Yanzhen Li, University of Bristol.
m.e:ai_research-multilingual-sprint: The next study was built before a single call was spent: 44 tasks across eight languages (264 prompt variants), split into high-risk exact-script tasks and controls; a fixed set of leading models; statistics that estimate uncertainty by resampling paired results; and generators for every table and figure. An adversarial audit from eight native-fluency perspectives replaced four homophone pairs that did not truly collapse. Whether to run the main study is still to be decided, so there are no multilingual results yet — and none are claimed.
m.e:company_design_events-brand-group-and-: Ahead of MWC Shanghai, an English brand push for the company: an English name and positioning, a plan for the English website and LinkedIn, and a checklist of show materials. The goal was simple — to arrive at an international show looking like one company, in English.
m.e:projects_code-atlas-claude-tab: A small Swift helper, about 200 lines, that registers ⌘T only while the ChatGPT Atlas browser is in front and routes it to Claude — switching to an existing tab, duplicating it or opening a new one — through the accessibility interface. The README is the fun part: it documents why seven standard approaches fail, because the browser’s new-tab page is a native view rather than a web page.
m.e:research_fpt-secular-term-cancellation: For a lazy ring with an antipodal shortcut, a ‘t·αᵗ’ term was suspected in the long-time tail of the first-passage distribution. It is not there. Three independent arguments show that its coefficient is identically zero: a partial-fraction sum rule; a trace of the term to an artefact of the generating-function inversion; and symmetry — the transient matrix is diagonalisable, so terms like t·λᵗ cannot occur for any parameters. Every identity was checked in 50-digit arithmetic and with exact rational kernels.
m.e:company_products-open-platform-launch: Within four days an open-source gateway for large language models (LLMs) became the company’s internal AI platform, the Yuexin Intelligent Open Platform. The gateway was chosen by reading the source code of two candidates rather than their brochures. The work covered a deployment runbook, white-labelling and full Chinese localisation of the admin interface, a mobile layout, and a self-service portal where colleagues sign in with Feishu (also known as Lark, a workplace chat-and-docs suite), get a key and see their own usage. Router retries, fallbacks and per-member budgets followed, and a pre-launch audit of model and permission boundaries closed the week.
m.e:school_teaching_service-festival-of-en: Presented BioPath as a PechaKucha at the University of Bristol Festival of Enterprise in the Arts Complex on 10 June 2026, with a printed poster for the showcase and a one-line promise: ‘Map in. Traps out. Proof attached.’ The talk was also built as a web deck, and that same night it became a subtitled pitch video (now on WeChat Channels). For the fellowship showcase three weeks later, a five-minute pre-recorded version followed.
m.e:self_media-bilingual-subtitle-engine: The local build of ffmpeg shipped without a subtitle renderer, so subtitles took another route: every bilingual cue is rendered as a transparent image and overlaid, in chunks of about ninety seconds processed in parallel, so an 8 min 44 s 4K clip renders in about two and a half minutes. A native Swift tool followed in July, and caption rules in August: at most two lines, 18 Chinese or 46 English characters per line, zero overlaps, and a terminology audit.
m.e:company_design_events-linkedin-company: Set up and launched the company’s LinkedIn page overnight on 10–11 June 2026, ahead of MWC Shanghai, a mobile-industry trade show: logo, cover, tagline, about text, website, industry and size, kept strictly on the Yuexin International brand. The artwork came from a brand pack made by a colleague; the work here was the page itself — and the decision that the company should have one before the show.
m.e:research_fpt-dpma-fold-theory: The ring’s double peak became a threshold theory. In the diffusive limit the walk becomes Brownian motion — continuous random movement — on an interval, with a sink standing for the shortcut. The first-passage density is a signed mixture of decay modes; a second peak needs at least three. With a central sink, the fold comes at a dimensionless sink strength of about 3.0764; near it, the peak–valley gap scales with the distance to it: power 1/2 in time, 3/2 in height. Five independent checks agree, including exact lattice calculations and a random-simulation (Monte Carlo) check with 400,000 walkers.
m.e:school_teaching_service-ambassador-pos: For open-day duty, designed an ‘Ask me about…’ Engineering Maths and AI ambassador poster in A4 and A3, an information-point poster for Royal Fort Garden, and square social posters in English and Chinese. They were built vector-first and audited like code: embedded fonts checked, page size verified, zero text overflow, and both QR codes re-verified module by module to point at the same handle on LinkedIn and Instagram.
m.e:company_design_events-mwc-shanghai-att: On the stand with the Yuexin International team — booth N4.E136 — for all three days of MWC Shanghai 2026, 24–26 June at the Shanghai New International Expo Centre. Before the show: meeting research from public sources, written up as 22 meeting dossiers, and 49 personalised meeting invitations sent through the show’s official app, each naming the booth and the day. After it: app chats, business cards and phone screenshots consolidated into one de-duplicated list of 214 leads, sorted into a follow-up order. It was the company’s first international show under its new English brand.
m.e:school_teaching_service-research-cultu: Proposed and organised a Research Culture Week session for the Faculty of Science and Engineering: ‘Strike Up New Connections’, a bowling social on 25 June 2026, open to PhD students, academic staff and professional-services colleagues. The work was the unglamorous kind — promotion and sign-ups (more than twenty within days), the venue booking, reconfirming attendance, a volunteer team for check-in — and an outcome report to the Research Culture team afterwards.
m.e:projects_code-pro-agent-bridge: A local MCP server (MCP is an open protocol that lets AI call outside tools) that turns ChatGPT’s developer mode into a bounded coding and hand-off surface for one repository: reading files, searching, exact edits, git inspection and safe verification commands. It extends the MIT-licensed open-source CodexPro by rebel0789 with hand-off from ChatGPT Pro to Claude Code, an AI coding agent, saved-session capture and hardened polling, and it is still in daily use. Credit where it is due: the foundation is upstream.
m.e:company_design_events-business-card-de: Designed Chinese and English business cards from the official website palette and the vector logo, generated as editable SVG and PDF files by script rather than by hand; then rebuilt the company’s bi-fold brochure as clean vectors, with its QR codes regenerated. The system was later packaged into an editable template so that colleagues could make their own cards — one design for the whole team.
m.e:ai_research-triangulated-audit: A reusable audit skill that attacks a research package from three angles over several rounds — a multi-agent workflow with access to the repository and tools, a strong external model, and a numerical and empirical arbiter — and settles every disagreement between models by computation rather than authority. The audit that motivated it showed why: a strong external model got a formula and a threshold wrong that the other participants got right; only the union plus the arbiter was complete; and a mistaken refutation forced a certification that made the result stronger.
m.e:school_teaching_service-dsfb-summer-pr: Over the summer of 2026, helped run a weekly in-person workshop supporting MSc Data Science for Business students through their group and individual dissertation projects — a maths PhD teaching AI projects to business students, one Tuesday at a time.
m.e:research_fpt-encounter-spectral-paper: A single-author working paper on when two diffusing particles that may react on meeting produce more than one reaction-time peak in finite models. Its tools include a reduction onto the reaction support, a sign-count gate (m peaks need at least 2m − 1 sign changes among the residues), an exact response to redistributing a fixed reactivity budget, and a continuum bridge built from refined two-dimensional lattice ladders and off-lattice Brownian dynamics. The headline conclusion: folds seen on coarse grids escape to the boundary of the admissible region in the continuum. Related work in progress looks at encounters with several reactive zones.
m.e:research_fpt-dpma-course: To understand the fold paper from the ground up, a single-file offline course was built around it: ten chapters that start from undergraduate analysis and linear algebra, build double-peak intuition from walker histograms, show how negative mode weights create peaks, and end with a slider for the sink’s strength that breaks the saddle-node fold live. Every chapter has self-tests. It is a study tool rather than course material — and the seed of the explainer in this chapter.
m.e:research_fpt-dpma-lean: The exact algebra of the fold paper — from Chebyshev product identities and the rank-one determinant to the closed-form splitting probability and the minimal three-mode theorem — was formalised in Lean 4, a proof assistant, with its mathlib library: 46 theorems across seven modules, with no ‘sorry’ (Lean’s placeholder for a missing proof) and only Lean’s three standard axioms. Numerical constants and analytic limits were left out of scope on purpose and checked numerically instead.
m.e:company_design_events-ops-codex-traini: Ran the operations team’s second round of hands-on agent training as lead trainer and technical judge. Each colleague demonstrated a real task running through an AI agent and was scored on time saved, quality, human review and reusability; the sessions covered browser and computer use, cross-app automation, memory and skills, scheduling and alerts. The cases were written up for reuse, and a case-based ‘AI work assistant’ boot camp was designed for the sales department.
m.e:company_products-ai-transformation-lea: In July 2026 a plan was drafted to bring the company’s scattered AI pilots into one programme, with department-level AI training. The training already delivered is described in Chapter 04.
m.e:school_teaching_service-tsr-allocation: In Mathematics: helping and moderating in Perspectives in Data Science and Perspectives in Mathematics, support sessions for Theory of Inference, marking for Quantum Computation and a tutorial group for Introduction to Pure Mathematics. In SEMT (the School of Engineering Mathematics and Technology): demonstrating and marking for Engineering Mathematics 1, group supervision in Mathematical and Data Modelling 3, labs in Statistical Computing and Empirical Methods, and teaching support for Foundations of AI. In CADE (the School of Civil, Aerospace and Design Engineering): teaching support for AI-Driven Design and Simulation, and the group research project of the MSc in Engineering with AI.
m.e:company_products-tender-intelligence: A daily agent that turns official public procurement notices into leads: it reads each notice, pulls out what is being bought and what is required, and writes a brief that a person can follow up. Everything with consequences — registering, buying documents, pricing, submitting — stays with people.
m.e:company_design_events-zhishu-logo-trus: An identity for Yuexin AI Nexus, the company’s enterprise-AI access-and-governance platform: two independent modules joined by one continuous, controlled central path — standing for identity, permission, budget, evidence and hand-off — in violet and amber, clearly apart from the existing red-blue-green ring. A final check tested legibility at small sizes; the delivery added app icons, print files and a record of how the mark was made.
m.e:company_products-governance-platform-l: The company’s unified AI access and governance platform went from local build to live in a week, launching on 31 July 2026. It is a self-built portal over an open-source gateway: keys issued by organisation and team, a list of allowed models, budgets and usage, a data-loss-prevention check, and an audit log kept as a hash chain, so that tampering with earlier entries can be detected; the gateway’s own admin interface is closed to the internet. Around launch it went through three kinds of check: several rounds of adversarial review by parallel AI agents; privacy ‘canary’ checks that planted synthetic identifiers and confirmed none survived in storage or logs; and formal production acceptance, with a receipt for every model.
m.e:research_fpt-dpma-pre-submitted: ‘Geometry-controlled folds of first-passage-time bimodality under localized absorption’ was submitted to Physical Review E as a single-author regular article on 30 July 2026. It is the first mathematics paper of the PhD: the geometry of a localized absorber decides whether a second arrival peak exists at all, and the peak is lost through a saddle-node fold — the peak meets a valley and both vanish — at a point that can be computed exactly. Every figure on this site that shows the effect is computed by code written for this site — exact master-equation curves and simulated walkers — not taken from the manuscript.
m.e:self_media-ecef-bilingual-channels-vid: As part of the Early Career Enterprise Fellowship (ECEF), the programme recorded an interview about moving from mathematics to a PhD in stochastic modelling, taking research into the real world, and trap placement with BioPath. It was edited into a 21-minute bilingual video with 309 independently audited caption cues and published on WeChat Channels in August 2026 under a Chinese title, ‘ECEF interview / Taking research into the real world’ — search 周易潇潇 in WeChat to watch.
m.e:ai_research-ai-escape-room: A concept for an AI and programming literacy escape room: an overconfident assistant hands the players code that looks right, and the only way out is to verify it — write the failing test, find the evidence — instead of trusting a confident answer. It is the verify-everything habit of the research, turned into a game for students.
m.e:company_design_events-llm-industry-tra: An in-person AI fundamentals session for technical and business staff on 5 August 2026 (the recording runs to 93 minutes) that used the SMS business as a lens on how the large-language-model industry works: a Chinese SMS is billed per 70 characters (67 per segment once a message runs long), a model per token (the unit of text a model reads and writes; depending on the model, one Chinese character can be less than a token or more than one), so the team’s habit of counting characters carries over once that conversion is learned. It ran from the value chain and the cost of tokens to retrieval (looking things up before answering), agents (AI that does tasks for you), hallucination (confident invention) and private deployment (running on your own servers) — and the six questions customers always ask. The materials — a 24-slide deck, a script for a 60-minute version and a handbook with an 81-term glossary, self-tests and customer-dialogue drills — were finalised the next day.
m.e:ai_research-ime-eval-v2-roadmap: The next study will measure typing effort and answer quality together, with a small typing experiment instead of a keystroke model; add about thirty homophone tasks with graded ambiguity; record the exact version of every model; and test why normalising the input first can lower quality. Claims will stay within the languages and tasks actually tested — the eight-language harness is built for the broader test.
m.e:ai_research-ukairs-acceptance: On 11 August 2026 UKAIRS accepted the paper for a poster session in the Emerging Research track. The reviews found the question genuinely interesting, the tool potentially useful and the inclusivity angle worth pursuing, and recommended leading with the ‘shi shi’ example and the three-layer analysis — encoding change, compression, tone loss. It is my first peer-reviewed AI paper, and I am first author.
m.e:research_fpt-fixed-budget-theorem-camp: For a reacting Brownian pair swept past stripes of catalyst, a first theorem (August 2026) showed that a small enough budget split across m stripes yields exactly m reaction-time peaks. A campaign of about 325 million simulated walkers tested it: all 48 cells of the two-stripe phase diagram gave exactly two peaks, a five-peak demonstration put five peaks at their designed times, and a three-dimensional spot check passed unchanged. An explicit bound on the admissible budget was then sharpened by 692 orders of magnitude, and the finite-dimensional core was formalised in Lean 4 (138 audited declarations, no ‘sorry’).
m.e:school_teaching_service-semt-pgr-rep-2: Bristol Students’ Union confirmed a second year as the Engineering Mathematics PGR (postgraduate research) Academic Rep on 18 August 2026. The new year began with helping bring new PhD reps into the team and keeping the School’s PhD community space open to newcomers.
m.e:ai_research-ukairs-poster-slot: The organisers assigned the poster to Wednesday 25 November 2026, 13:15–14:15, in Lunch & Poster Session 3, and sent the presentation guidance. The public poster list shows it as #181 under ‘F. Synergistic Human–AI Collaboration’, Emerging Research, Xiaoxiao Zhouyi, University of Bristol.
m.e:prior_site_design-first-passage-canvas: The first design for this site, in August 2026, was a canvas of eight artboards: a particle-field hero, a prologue, a memory galaxy, a two-trajectory timeline, a digital twin and a research page. Reopened a month later, it earned a blunt verdict — no feeling of light and gradient, and no way to see the achievements — and a clearer brief followed: more light, achievements you can see, real interaction, and a summing-up of everything so far. The luminous plate on the front page, with the achievements beside it, is the answer.
m.e:self_media-wechat-studio-kickoff: It publishes to WeChat Channels (WeChat’s short-video feed) and a WeChat Official Account (its long-form channel). In October and November 2026 they carried four to-camera videos and long-form articles: figures are checked before they go in, and the sources are listed at the end. A scan of the archive that could pause and pick up again covered 3,943 of the 3,947 videos and found speech in 1,052 — and only such counts are ever published. The channel’s name is 周易潇潇.
m.e:company_design_events-wwc-materials-de: Over four days and three design rounds, I designed the kit for the Wholesale World Congress (WWC), a telecoms trade show in Madrid: five kinds of one-pager, led by an English sheet headlined ‘Intelligence. Delivered.’; then, after the team’s prep meeting, three double-sided A4 leaflets in English and Chinese (a QR code on the back of each), an English company introduction, a supplier questionnaire and four business cards for the delegation. Everything was built through an HTML-to-PDF pipeline, and every QR code was decode-tested before the print files went out on 8 September.
m.e:company_design_events-connect-contact-: A contact microsite for the Wholesale World Congress delegation, reached from a 19 mm QR code on each business card: a page per person with messaging, LinkedIn, email, website and save-contact links, plus a browser-based card editor so that each person can maintain their own. It went live on the company’s connect subdomain and was decode-tested card by card.
m.e:research_fpt-reproduction-releases: Everything behind the fixed-budget paper (a manuscript in preparation) is public and checkable: simulation, analysis and plotting code, machine-readable numerical records, interval-arithmetic certificates (calculations with rigorous error bounds), the Lean 4 proof files (Lean 4 is a proof assistant) and the job records from Isambard 3 (a UK national supercomputer), all pinned by SHA-256 checksums, so a change to any file would show. Five releases went out between 8 and 26 September 2026 as the paper was rebuilt — about 1,466 files in the latest, including 100 Python scripts, 27 Lean files and 1,198 JSON records. Anyone can re-run the numbers without asking.
m.e:school_teaching_service-dsfb-second-ma: In September 2026, second-marked a set of MSc Data Science for Business dissertations, including a group project, following the programme’s new marking guidance and agreeing final marks for the written component with the first markers.
m.e:company_design_events-sms-market-map-p: An interactive, bilingual map of how enterprises buy SMS and where delivery really succeeds. It follows one text message from a business to a phone — who carries it, which way the money and the delivery receipts travel, and what ‘delivered’ can mean — then maps who buys, what they need and how they choose. It began as a whiteboard sketch and became a dependency-free web page the same day, revised after three AI review passes on content, usability and release safety. The version on this site was rebuilt for a general reader.
m.e:company_design_events-wwc-madrid-onsit: With the company’s four-person team at the Wholesale World Congress 2026 in Madrid (16–18 September), the carrier-wholesale industry’s annual meeting, looking for partners in SMS routes, one-time passcodes, RCS (richer mobile messaging) and eSIM (a digital SIM). The company had no stand of its own; the team met partners at theirs. Before the show, meeting requests went to 25 operators and messaging hubs. On site: a live bilingual schedule of 22 meeting slots, kept in Madrid and Beijing time, and 31 exhibitor dossiers written into the team knowledge base during the show. Then back to Bristol, straight into the new academic year — from trade floor to lecture theatre.
m.e:company_products-yuexin-chat-launch: In one day, an assistant for company staff was built and launched on the company’s model gateway. Colleagues sign in with Feishu and are provisioned automatically, with a personal monthly quota and self-serve API keys. The web app streams its answers, folds away the model’s reasoning, renders Markdown and maths, accepts images and has light and dark themes; a Windows desktop client shipped alongside it, with a download page. Before release it went through three parallel security reviews and an independent review by a second model.
m.e:school_teaching_service-careers-blog-f: The University of Bristol Careers Service published a Student Founder Spotlight on 21 September 2026 — ‘From strawberry patch to PhD: how engineering maths inspired BioPath’ — on a PhD researcher in Engineering Mathematics building a trap-placement optimisation tool for pest control, and on the route through New Enterprise and the Early Career Enterprise Fellowship to the Festival of Enterprise.
m.e:projects_code-bristol-law-career-roadm: A responsive, editorial-style Chinese guide for Bristol Master of Laws (LLM) students planning a legal career back in China in 2026–27: chapter navigation, full-text search, filterable events and recruitment, a four-week practice plan, ten copy-ready templates, dated updates on official AI products and 42 primary sources — with no analytics and no backend. The same editorial language as the housing map: a small shelf of Bristol guides.
m.e:company_products-yuexin-chat-desktop-a: The desktop client that shipped with the assistant is being rebuilt as a coding and office agent: an open-source agent engine underneath, a Yuexin interface on top. Planned for the next rounds: a built-in browser and terminal, scheduled tasks, skills, and acting in Feishu, the company’s workplace suite, on the person’s behalf — with a confirmation before every send, share or approval. It is still in development; these are plans, not shipped features.
m.e:research_fpt-fixed-budget-paper: ‘Programmable multimodality and saddle-node loss of reaction-time peaks under a fixed catalyst budget’ is a single-author manuscript in preparation. A fixed amount of static catalyst, split into thin stripes along the path of a reacting Brownian pair, programs the reaction-time density: at weak noise each stripe removes a fixed fraction of the arriving pairs — a stick-breaking law — so there is exactly one peak per stripe, and designs with prescribed peak times and weights exist, are locally unique and can be found by Newton’s method. Fixed-width stripes can instead lose a late peak through a saddle-node bifurcation, certified by interval arithmetic in test cases. The finite-dimensional and calculus core is checked in Lean 4; the stochastic parts are proved by hand.
m.e:school_teaching_service-offline-teachi: For the first tutorial of Introduction to Pure Mathematics, a tablet-first web app was built and tested in a day: an English-first teaching script and a bilingual reference library of 39 topics — overviews, prerequisites and strategies — that works offline, with mathematics typeset locally and no tracking of any kind. The same site now carries a Linear Algebra section.
m.e:school_teaching_service-scem-week1-lab: Demonstrated the Week 1 R lab for the MSc unit Statistical Computing and Empirical Methods on 23 September 2026 — a unit taken as an MSc student two years earlier — after preparing a bilingual teaching pack that works through all 25 Week 1 exercises.
m.e:school_teaching_service-linear-algebra: Taught the year’s first Linear Algebra tutorial to a group of new undergraduates on 25 September 2026, with printed worksheet sets prepared the day before — a group added to the year’s teaching in September.
m.e:prior_site_design-brief-2026-09-28: The site you are reading draws the record as a first-passage process, the mathematics of the PhD: random walkers leave Tianjin and stop when they first reach an item, on a timeline from 2021 to now, that matches what you search for. It replaces the page that, since April 2026, simply forwarded zhouyixiaoxiao.com to LinkedIn. It was designed to one written specification and built with AI coding agents; every fact comes from a verified, privacy-tagged record, and nothing private shipped.
m.e:ai_research-ukairs-presentation: UKAIRS 2026, the UK AI Research Symposium: 24–25 November 2026, John McIntyre Conference Centre, Edinburgh; poster #181 in the poster session of Wednesday 25 November, 13:15–14:15. The plan, written into the paper, is a side-by-side demo — the native prompt, its keyboard-friendly variant, the agent’s response, the grade and the effort estimate — so that visitors can toggle from routine prompts to homophone traps and watch where meaning collapses. Chapter 02 of this site is an early version of that demo.
m.e:ai_research-fusion-challenge: The Fusion Equilibrium Challenge, in the NeurIPS 2026 Competition Track, asks for the magnetic flux map of a tokamak (a fusion device) to be predicted from its coil currents and Thomson-scattering profiles (laser measurements of the plasma), without magnetic sensors. In the blind Final, with results announced on 14 November 2026, the solo entry took second place in Challenge 1, on DIII-D, with a score of 0.997253, and 13th place in Challenge 2, zero-shot transfer to MAST. The invited 15-minute talk at the competition workshop in Atlanta on 12 December 2026 is an interactive web page rather than slides. The code is public under the MIT licence.
